beats.t: Morning never came beneath the tower. The sky had stopped at gray.
They sat in a circle among fallen bricks. No one suggested getting up first.
Yeoni looked down at their feet. A white sock on the left, a gray one on the right. Mismatched.
(Wear matching socks. Who said that? Not Mom. Mom doesn't say things like that.)
Strange. The voice of that scolding remained in their ears.
Low, sounding put-upon, with a little laughter mixed in. No face came with it.
Looking at your socks?
Yes. I think someone told me to wear matching ones.
Mr. Cat. He hated your mismatched socks more than anyone.
Mr. Cat. Is he Neo? In my note?
Yes. A cat at first, then human. We kept calling him Mr. Cat out of habit.
Yeoni opened their notebook again. They no longer knew how many times.
The same words remained plainly on the page. Even in a different form, Neo. On my side.
I've been thinking too. That cat... I think he lit a fire with my matches once. Or did I light it for him?
All I have left is a white umbrella. A rainy bus stop, a folded white umbrella. The voice saying, Too late.
The three offered one fragment each. The fragments didn't fit.
Cat, silver hair, umbrella, socks. The words remained, but they wouldn't join into one face.
Different appearances, all the same person? Why can't I recognize any of them?
Yes. The same person as a cat and as a human. The sock lectures stayed the same too.
Yeoni couldn't laugh. It felt as though everyone knew someone only they didn't.
No. Everyone half knew someone they didn't know at all.
I must be a terrible person. I wrote that he's on my side, and I don't know his face.
Yeoni took out their phone. Even in the world of destiny, its screen lit up.
An app icon: a little star set above a moonlit door. The same as the night it first appeared.
Yeoni tapped customer support. They hadn't known it could make calls. But there was a button: Call.
[ Customer Support: Universe ] [ Agents: None · Queue Position: ∞ ]
Same as ever. Definitely the app I gave one star.
The ringing went on and on. No one answered. Yeoni didn't hang up. Holding it to their ear made them feel strangely less alone.
(Someone must have called like this every day too. An unanswered phone. Trying to find someone.)
The infinity symbol in the queue flickered briefly. It nearly became a number, then returned to infinity.
Yeoni didn't see. Too tired to look at the screen, they had closed their eyes.
[ Queue Position: ∞ ] ...9,999... ∞
Their pocket warmed. Not the phone. Beside it, a card they had carried for a long time.
Dark blue, with stars patterned on the back. Yeoni's birth card.
This one. It never would turn over.
The card stirred on its own, very slowly in their palm. The stars turned downward, and the picture faced up.
[ Birth Card · 17 · The Star ]
A waterside beneath the night sky. A woman knelt, pouring from two pitchers.
One into water, one onto land. Above her, one great star and seven small ones.
The Star. The card after the Tower. The one that rises after everything has fallen.
I know this card. It was in my room. The day my umbrella blew inside out, this picture was on the floor.
The night they first opened destiny's door returned to mind. The bus card they'd given one star, the inside-out umbrella, cards scattered on the floor.
Among them, the Star. That memory remained unerased.
The card poured out light. The gray sky split, and night descended.
Water rose among the fallen bricks, clear and ankle deep. Stars reflected in it.
Where are we? Inside the card?
Inside your card, Yeoni. Usually only its owner can enter a birth card. Perhaps being together lets us come in together.
The woman from the card wasn't by the water. Only two pitchers stood there: one empty, one full.
Two pitchers. One pours into the water, one onto the land.
The Star gives back what it receives. What was received to the water; what can be shared to the earth.
Seo Hanbi lifted the full pitcher. Heavy. Rain sounded inside it, the sound that matched her name.
This is my rain. The rain I released from the ledger. It all gathered here.
Yeoni. Give me your hand. The scrape from the tower.
It's nothing.
Then it should heal even faster.
Seo Hanbi tilted the pitcher. Fine rain fell onto Yeoni's palm.
It wasn't cold. The scrape closed very slowly. Not even a scab remained.
Carrying the pitcher, Seo Hanbi went around the group. Moka's singed whiskers. Yundal's trembling palm.
Wherever the rain touched, wounds vanished one by one.
The place where I used the Void doesn't hurt. That's never happened before.
My whiskers grew back. Hanbi, if you could do this, why not sooner?
Before, I only knew how to collect.
The water in the pitcher diminished a little. Faint ledger-ink stains on the back of Seo Hanbi's hand washed away with it.
She looked at them for a long time without speaking.
The final raindrop fell onto Yeoni's left hand.
The hand they had kept clenched since the tower. Something glittered between their fingers.
A golden thread unraveled from Neo's coat. When rain touched it, the light trapped inside came alive.
Then it seeped into Yeoni's palm. It hadn't vanished. It had entered.
Hot. My chest. No, inside my chest.
Wait. Let me look at your Four Pillars again.
[ Year: Im-o · Month: Byeong-o · Day: Eulhae · Hour: □-Chen ] 7/8 · Faint Metal within the Day's Eul
There's Metal inside your Day Master. Inside Eul. That means a combination is holding.
Combination? Compatibility again?
Actual compatibility this time. Eul and Gyeong are drawn toward each other. Even after Gyeong left its column, Eul held on to a piece.
Yundal removed his glove. A golden ray was caught inside the Void in his palm too.
Light that had broken away as Neo was swallowed at the tower. Yundal's Void had held that single strand.
I had one too. I couldn't find the moment to tell you. You were crying so much.
Then Black Moon didn't eat all of him. Pieces remain. One with me, one with Yundal.
And you're Bharani, Yeoni. We saw it in the Vedic sky. The star that bears. A vessel contains. Bearing protects.
Black Moon called you a vessel. If Mr. Cat is already inside that vessel, there's no room for Black Moon.
Yeoni laid a hand on their chest. There was a warm spot. They didn't know who he was, but they knew that place existed.
I don't remember. But this handwriting is mine. This hand is mine too. If I won't trust what I wrote, who will?
Yeoni opened a fresh page and pulled the pen cap off with their teeth. They wrote down each fragment the others offered.
[ Neo · Cat, then human · Silver hair · Lots of scolding · Socks · Umbrella · Once arrived late · On my side ]
Do we really need 'lots of scolding'?
The most reliable information we have. Everyone remembers it.
Add one more. Extremely jealous of me.
Needs verification. Someone told me to believe only half of what Yundal says.
Mr. Cat said that too.
Everyone laughed. The first laughter since coming down from the tower. It spread over the star pool, making its reflected stars tremble.
At the bottom of the page, Yeoni added one more line. This time, no one dictated it. It was their own sentence.
[ Going to find him. Even without remembering. Trust my handwriting. ]
That line is a far better ledger than mine.
I won't be someone who only gets rescued again. I'll follow my own handwriting and choose our ending myself.
It's a note, not a ledger. A note with nothing to repay.
The last of the pitcher's water fell into the star pool. The reflected stars began shifting, one by one.
They formed a path toward Card Eighteen.
Next is the Moon. Eighteen. A card of deception. Not everything you see is real.
A card Black Moon would like.
If it's a card of lies, I can burn it all. I've still got two matches.
Save those two carefully, Moka. The Sun is the very next card.
Sun? That's my department. Just wait, Moon.
Suddenly you're looking impressive, Moka. One more star for you.
As Yeoni stood, they looked into the pool. Their face reflected back: swollen eyes, hair a mess.
But the Yeoni in the water was smiling. Yeoni wasn't. The reflected mouth lifted once, then twice.
As though practicing how to smile. Only on the third attempt did it resemble Yeoni's smile.
Hanbi. Look. My face...
Seo Hanbi looked into the pool and went white.
She had seen that smile before. In the first spring, at the rainy bus stop.
